# WhatCyber

> WhatCyber is a threat intelligence site. It tracks more than 270,000 CVEs from the National Vulnerability Database, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, threat actor profiles based on MITRE ATT&CK, and cybersecurity news from trusted sources. Every page is plain HTML that can be read without JavaScript, shows the date of its latest entry, and links to the primary source.

The pages below answer the questions people most often ask about vulnerabilities: which flaws are being exploited, how severe a CVE is, which vendors and products are affected, and which threat groups are active.

## Hubs

- [CISA KEV catalog](https://www.whatcyber.com/cisa-kev): the vulnerabilities CISA has confirmed are exploited in the wild, newest first, with due dates and ransomware use. Includes a short FAQ on how the catalog works.
- [Latest CVEs](https://www.whatcyber.com/cve): newly published CVEs with CVSS severity scores.
- [Threat actors](https://www.whatcyber.com/threat-actors): profiles of more than 170 threat groups, with aliases and descriptions from MITRE ATT&CK.
- [Vulnerabilities by vendor](https://www.whatcyber.com/vendors): the 100 vendors with the most CVEs, each with its newest CVEs, exploited vulnerabilities and most common weaknesses.
- [Common software weaknesses (CWE)](https://www.whatcyber.com/cwe): the 50 weaknesses behind the most CVEs, with how many are known to be exploited.
- [Threat feed](https://www.whatcyber.com/threatfeed): cybersecurity news aggregated from trusted sources.
- [Blog](https://www.whatcyber.com/blog): analysis and guides on vulnerabilities and threat intelligence.

## Tools

- [CVSS calculator](https://www.whatcyber.com/tools/cvss-calculator): one calculator with a switch between CVSS v4.0 and v3.1. It works out the score from the metrics, shows the severity rating and the vector string, and (for v3) loads the vector of any published CVE to check its score.

## Page patterns

- CVE page: https://www.whatcyber.com/cve/CVE-YYYY-NNNN. A plain summary, CVSS and EPSS scores, KEV status and due date, timeline, weaknesses, affected products, references and related news. Example: https://www.whatcyber.com/cve/CVE-2024-3400
- Threat actor page: https://www.whatcyber.com/threat-actors/<name>, for example https://www.whatcyber.com/threat-actors/apt28
- Vendor page: https://www.whatcyber.com/vendors/<vendor>, for example https://www.whatcyber.com/vendors/fortinet
- Product page: https://www.whatcyber.com/vendors/<vendor>/<product>, for example https://www.whatcyber.com/vendors/fortinet/fortios. Products with known exploited vulnerabilities only.
- Weakness page: https://www.whatcyber.com/cwe/CWE-<number>, for example https://www.whatcyber.com/cwe/CWE-79

## Data sources

- [CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog): which CVEs are exploited, due dates, ransomware use
- [National Vulnerability Database](https://nvd.nist.gov/): CVE records, CVSS scores, weaknesses and affected products
- [FIRST EPSS](https://www.first.org/epss/): the probability that a CVE will be exploited in the next 30 days
- [MITRE ATT&CK groups](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/): threat actor names, aliases and descriptions
- [MITRE CWE](https://cwe.mitre.org/): weakness names and descriptions
